reconcile.note: John Gill defends Abraham's marriage to his paternal half-sister Sarah as lawful in that earlier era, before Leviticus later forbade such unions.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is incest forbidden?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/incest.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife
sides.verseText: Moreover she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.

sides.snippet: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother
sides.verseText: \"'You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother, whether born at home, or born abroad.
